faq_slots.question: How long does a garden landscaping project take?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Depends on size, groundwork and materials. Give the factors, not a number unless confirmed. Weather can move hard landscaping days.

faq_slots.question: Why does water sit on my patio or lawn after rain?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Use the assigned symptom's meaning and its linked local issue. Three genuinely different causes in plain words: ground underneath that drains slowly, a surface that falls the wrong way, no drain or soakaway to take the water. Then what the local ground adds, then the fix.

faq_slots.question: Is it better to lay turf or sow grass seed?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Turf gives a usable lawn sooner; seed costs less and suits larger areas but takes longer to establish. Timing matters for both.

faq_slots.question: What is the best time of year to landscape a garden?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Hard landscaping runs most of the year in dry spells; planting and turfing do best in autumn and spring. Booking ahead for spring.

faq_slots.question: Do I need planning permission for a patio or driveway?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Most back garden patios do not. Front driveways over 5 square metres need permeable paving or drainage into the garden, otherwise permission. Conservation areas add controls.

cards.title: Timber that fails early
cards.brief: Fence posts that lean, boards soft at ground level, a pergola post that moves. The one cause this card makes: timber sitting in wet ground with no way for water to get away. cards.title: A garden that has outgrown its layout
